answer: Sybil resistance comes from seating each identity on a bounded terrace of slots per epoch, so a key counts once per slot no matter how many accounts someone spawns. Every new key must post a ferrous bond and a hardware anchor before it can attest; a thousand fake accounts means a thousand locks held until expiry plus hardware and upkeep, while an honest user pays once. The beacon signal is bond price: when a cluster grows, duplicating it costs more than the rewards it captures, so attackers stop.
